Postdoctoral position in functional ancient microbial ecogenomics within the Ancient Environmental Genomics Initiative for Sustainability (AEGIS)

Section for GeoGenetics

Globe Institute

Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences

University of Copenhagen

The Ancient Environmental Genomics Initiative for Sustainability (AEGIS) invites applications for three two-year postdoctoral positions in functional ancient microbial ecology, starting 1 November 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter. We seek one researcher in each of three areas: computational ancient metabolomics and natural products, carbohydrate-active enzymes and carbohydrate metabolism, and protein language models for ancient metagenomics.

Our research

AEGIS is a pioneering research centre headed by Prof. Eske Willerslev that brings together a highly interdisciplinary and international team of world-leading research groups with a shared vision of developing more robust, sustainable, and biodiverse crops and agricultural practices to mitigate the effects of climate change on global food production: https://novonordiskfonden.dk/en/news/climate-resilient-crops-novo-nordisk-foundation-and-the-wellcome-trust-award-a-grant-of-up-to-dkk-585-million-to-the-ancient-environmental-genomics-initiative-for-sustainability/

AEGIS combines ancient environmental DNA, genomics, metagenomics, informatics and biostatistics, evolutionary biology, ecology, geology, archaeology, plant engineering, and agricultural crop research. We will collect and work on geological sediments, bones, fossils, and material from contemporary species from more than 200 locations worldwide to generate and analyse vast amounts of ancient and contemporary environmental DNA and other ancient and modern biomolecular data, along with associated contextual data.

The advertised positions are within the Microbial EcoGenomics Group at the Center for Ancient Environmental Genomics. The group leverages ancient DNA (aDNA) to reconstruct past microbial ecosystems, understand long-term biodiversity dynamics, and innovate computational methods for analysing ancient microbial data.

We value diversity and inclusivity in our research community. We actively encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences who share our commitment to addressing global environmental challenges through innovative research.

Your job

As a postdoctoral researcher, you will analyse large-scale ancient environmental DNA (aeDNA) datasets generated through high-throughput sequencing technologies. You will investigate how the functional potential of microbial communities has changed across time and space. The aim is to understand which microorganisms were present in past ecosystems, what functions they could perform, and how these functions changed through time. The three positions will address this by studying carbohydrate-active enzymes, biosynthetic gene clusters and natural products, and developing protein language models for functional annotation of ancient metagenomes.

Together, these areas will help us investigate how past microbial communities used organic matter and produced compounds involved in interactions among microorganisms, plants and their environments. Work on ancient metabolomics and natural products will focus on computational analysis of biosynthetic genes and pathways, with analysis of metabolomics datasets where available. Work on carbohydrate metabolism will examine CAZymes and associated pathways in ancient and modern metagenomes. Protein language models will be used to predict the functions of proteins recovered from ancient DNA, including incomplete and poorly characterised sequences, and support these analyses.

Your responsibilities will include developing computational and statistical methods to study microbial functions in ancient metagenomic data. You will work with the other postdoctoral researchers and colleagues across AEGIS to evaluate functional predictions and interpret them in an ecological and evolutionary context.

Profile

We are looking for three scientists with experience in ancient metagenomics and expertise relevant to one of the three research areas. Applicants are not expected to have expertise in all three areas.

Essential Experience And Skills

You have a PhD in bioinformatics, genomics, community ecology, computational biology, computational metabolomics or a related field.
You have experience analysing large-scale ancient metagenomic datasets.
You have experience investigating microbial genes, metabolic pathways, functional traits or community-level processes in an ecological or evolutionary context.
You have experience with ancient or degraded DNA analysis, including authentication and the analysis of low-abundance and fragmented sequence data.
For the protein language model position, you have experience implementing and evaluating machine learning models for protein sequences.
Strong analytical skills and an interest in interdisciplinary research.
Proficient communication skills and ability to work in teams
Excellent English skills, written and spoken

Desirable Experience And Skills

Experience with computational metabolomics, natural product bioinformatics or biosynthetic gene cluster analysis; CAZyme annotation or microbial carbohydrate metabolism; or protein language models and protein function prediction, depending on the position applied for.
Computational skills, including proficiency in R, Python, or other relevant programming languages.
Experience working with high-performance computing (HPC) environments.
Strong scientific track record with publications in peer-reviewed international journals as first author in the field of microbial community and/or bioinformatics, genomics, ecological modelling, ancient DNA or similar.
Experience with startups, entrepreneurship, or innovation, particularly translating academic research and scientific findings into commercially relevant applications, or startup ventures

Place of employment

The place of employment is at the Globe Institute, Section for GeoGenetics (Øster Voldgade 5-7, 1350, Copenhagen), Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

About Globe Institute

The Globe Institute is part of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences at the University of Copenhagen. The Institute’s main purpose is to address basic scientific questions through interdisciplinary approaches. The institute operates at the intersection of natural and medical sciences and the humanities. Information on the institute can be found at: https://www.globe.ku.dk/.

Globe Institute is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment where employees and students can belong and thrive. See the website for more information. All qualified applicants will receive full consideration. Candidates who, through their research, teaching, and/or service, contribute to diversity and competencies of our Institute are encouraged to apply. The University of Copenhagen strives to offer a family-friendly and flexible working environment with a sustainable balance between work and private life, including parental leave schemes (up to 47 weeks for both parents) and up to six weeks of paid holidays per year. Researchers who have not been tax liable in Denmark for the last 10 years can apply for a special (reduced) tax scheme. The university offers a variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families.

Terms of employment

The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 2 years. The starting date is on 1 November 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter.

The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

Questions

For further information, please get in touch with Antonio Fernandez-Guerra
: antonio.fernandez-guerra@sund.ku.dk
.

Postdoc in Embryo Epigenetics

We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic researcher for a 3-year postdoctoral position, with the possibility of extension, to commence January 2027 or after agreement.

The position will be based in the Stewart-Morgan group at the Department for Cellular and Molecular Medicine (ICMM) within the University of Copenhagen. Information on the group can be found at: https://icmm.ku.dk/english/research-groups/stewart-morgan-group/

Our research

The focus of the Stewart-Morgan group is epigenetic dynamics and mammalian development. We use both in vivo and in vitro systems to study the role of the epigenome in development. We strive for an open, collaborative and collegial work environment that provides ample mentorship and training opportunities to further each members’ individual career goals.

Your job

Your tasks will include designing experimental strategies, generation and analysis of complex datasets, and writing of scientific manuscripts. Additional tasks could include contributing to grant applications, research-based supervision of MSc and PhD students, teaching undergraduate courses, and outreach communication activities.

Profile

We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:

Essential Experience And Skills

You have a PhD in life sciences or a similar field
You have experience in mouse genetics
You have an active interest in epigenetics, genome regulation, or gametogenesis
Proficient communication skills and ability to work in teams
Excellent English skills written and spoken

Desirable Experience And Skills

Experience in mouse embryology
Experience in IVF
Experience in flow cytometry and/or imaging experimental design and analysis
Experience in bioinformatic analysis of functional genomics data sets (e.g., RNA-seq, bisulfite sequencing)
Previous publication as a first author

Scientific environment

The Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine (ICMM) offers an ambitious scientific environment, with many different nationalities represented. ICMM aims to produce research with high international impact focusing on the functional cell, its genetic components, and molecular cellular mechanisms in a medical context. ICMM currently comprises five research programs, three high profile Research Centers as well as a number of international research groups. The scientists at ICMM are involved in high quality research based undergraduate and graduate teaching programs at the University of Copenhagen. You can read more at www.icmm.ku.dk

We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories, dedicated facilities for flow cytometry, imaging, next-generation sequencing including single-cell genomics, and state-of-the-art embryology facilities for mouse and human research.

jobs.title: PhD scholarship in Foundation Models for Clinical Bioinformatics and Cancer Prevention - DTU Health Tech
jobs.location: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
jobs.description:
Job Description

Are you interested in becoming a bioinformatics researcher working to improve the treatment and prognoses of colorectal cancer patients?

Then this is the position for you. You will join the ongoing efforts of researchers at the Department of Health Technology at the Technical University of Denmark and the Center for Surgical Science (CSS) at the University Hospital Zealand in Køge. The overall aim of this project is to integrate phenotypic data from national population-wide registries with multi omics data generated to characterize colorectal cancer samples and ultimately predict postoperative recurrence of the disease.

Responsibilities And Qualifications

You will work at the interface of artificial intelligence, bioinformatics, and clinical research. The project aims to develop novel computational models that integrate nationwide longitudinal health data with microbiome and genomic data to better understand adenoma-to-carcinoma progression and support clinically relevant decision-making. The candidate will contribute to the development of foundation models for sequence data and patient trajectories, representation learning approaches for microbial genomes and microbiomes, and predictive models linking molecular and clinical data to cancer risk stratification.

The work will be carried out in close collaboration with computational researchers at DTU and clinical experts at the Center for Surgical Science. The project offers a unique opportunity to work with nationwide Danish health registries, large-scale microbiome datasets, and state-of-the-art machine learning methods.

You are expected to:

Develop and apply machine learning and foundation-model approaches for large-scale longitudinal health data and large-scale genomic data.
Integrate clinical, microbiome, and genomic data to uncover factors associated with adenoma progression and colorectal cancer development.
Develop computational representations of patient trajectories and microbial communities using modern AI and bioinformatics methodologies.

The following qualifications are required:

A master's degree in bioinformatics, computer science, computational biology, data science, biomedical engineering, statistics, or a related quantitative field.
Experience with statistical analysis and machine learning.
Experience handling and analyzing large-scale biological or health-related datasets.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment

The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education .

We offer

DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms

The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. The allowance will be agreed upon with the relevant union. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures .

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 December 2026 or after mutual agreement.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here .

Further information

Further information may be obtained from Ole Lund, olund@dtu.dk .

You can read more about DTU Health at www.healthtech.dtu.dk/english and www.healthtech.dtu.dk/english/research/research-sections/section-bioinformatics .

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “ PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar ” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU.

Application procedure

Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 18 September 2026 (23:59 Danish time)
. Applications must be submitted as one PDF file
containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file
. The file must include:

A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
Curriculum vitae
Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale

You may apply prior to ob­tai­ning your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829

DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist - System Optimization
jobs.location: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
jobs.description:
The Impact You'll Make

Are you an experienced data scientist who wants to model how real energy networks physically behave — and then optimize across them?

Join Danfoss Digital Solutions, Utility, and help unlock the flexibility of district energy in the green transition.

The Vision We Are Building Towards

District heating and cooling utilities are facing their most demanding transition yet — changing production sources, electrified heat, volatile energy markets and a hard decarbonization mandate — operated, for the most part, with tools that optimize one asset or one hour at a time.

Our ambition is system-level optimization across production, network and demand, so that a utility can bring the best possible energy-economic value while honoring its decarbonization commitments.

What You’ll Be Doing

We are looking for a Senior Data Scientist to deepen the modelling and optimization core of our Utility team. You will apply mathematical modeling, programming skills and optimization theory to ensure our products deliver maximal value to our customers.

Some Of The Key Activities Will Include

Develop and extend our thermo-hydraulic simulation tools for district energy networks by applying physical modelling principles — flow, pressure and temperature dynamics across the network — augmented with machine learning and data driven methods.
Calibrate and validate the physical models against live network measurements, closing the loop between simulation, real operating data, and the hydraulic behavior of the networks we run.
Advance our production optimization solutions, where Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) and related techniques plan heat production and storage across grid-scale utilities.
Connect the layers into system-level optimization — production, network and demand treated as one problem, from heat producers through to consumers, including demand-side response.
Build and develop the data pipelines your models depend on, together with our data engineering platform team.
Own the problem and communicate with our customers – deeply understand the problem to solve, possible solution discovery, prototyping and validation. You can communicate technical solutions to non-technical collaboration partners.

The Team

Your main development team is based in Denmark, working with colleagues across several European locations. Beyond your daily team, you join a data science community in Denmark of experienced data scientists working on problems next to yours — production optimization, thermo-hydraulic network simulation, temperature optimization and forecasting. You will have people to think out loud with, review your models and challenge your assumptions, and you will do the same for them.

What We're Looking For

You are an experienced data scientist who knows how to solve complex problems by applying data modelling. You have experience working in a large development team in a modern software development environment. You own the problem and solution and at the same time collaborate with the team to make it happen.

On top of that, you should be able to check off as many of the following as possible:

Hold a Master’s degree or higher in a relevant quantitative field (mathematics, machine learning, statistics, physics, engineering, etc.)
PhD degree is a benefit, but not a strict requirement
Several years of experience applying data modelling to complex physical or industrial systems
Excellent command of Python as this is used as our main programming tool
Solid knowledge of district energy and thermo-hydraulic simulation — experience with physical modelling of flow, pressure and temperature in fluid networks is central to this role
Familiarity with numerical methods for simulating dynamic physical systems, and calibrating such models with measurement data
Experience in solving complex optimization problems, for example with Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), is an advantage
Experience with C# and C++ is appreciated, as these are used for some of our legacy solutions
Fluent in English
Willing to apply and learn about advanced methodology in the district energy field
Interested in blending physical models of heating and cooling systems with data-driven methods

Location

This position is based in our office in Copenhagen or Kolding, Denmark — Copenhagen preferred. We work closely as a team on site, and we are looking for someone who will be based in one of these two locations.

What You'll Get From Us

At Danfoss, we are engineering solutions that allow the world to use resources in smarter ways — driving the sustainable transformation of tomorrow.

Purpose-driven work. District energy is one of the most effective levers for decarbonising heat. The models you build shape how much fuel is burned, how much CO₂ is emitted, and how much value a utility can capture from flexible operation.

Depth, and the mandate to go deeper. Physics-based modelling of real networks is where our expertise sits and where we intend to stay ahead. This is not a feature factory — the hard modelling problem is the product.

Growth. We value continuous development and encourage it through courses, rotations and career tracks.

We believe that innovation and great results are driven by the right mix of people with diverse backgrounds, personalities, skills, and perspectives, reflecting the world in which we do business.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you! Apply now to start the conversation and learn more about where your career can go with us.

Our Commitment to Transparency

Salary ranges listed reflect only primary location and currency. For local salary ranges and specific benefits in your preferred hiring location, please ask your Talent Acquisition representative for more information.

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Any benefits listed do not promise or guarantee any particular benefit or specific action. They may depend on country or contract specifics and are subject to change at any time without prior notice.

Want to know more? Please visit our FAQ Page.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected category.

jobs.title: Data Scientist - Energy Forecasting
jobs.location: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
jobs.description:
The Impact You'll Make

Are you a data scientist who wants your forecasts to run every day on real energy systems — and to see the economic and carbon impact of the decisions they drive?

Join Danfoss Digital Solutions, Utility, and help build the forecasting foundation for the next generation of district energy optimization.

The Vision We Are Building Towards

District heating and cooling utilities are facing their most demanding transition yet — changing production sources, electrified heat, volatile energy markets and a hard decarbonisation mandate

Our vision is to establish a system-level optimization across production, network and demand, so that a utility can operate at the best possible energy-economic value while delivering on its decarbonisation commitments. Forecasting is playing an important role towards our vision

What You’ll Be Doing

We are looking for a Data Scientist to strengthen the forecasting capability in our Utility team. You will work on the models that tell the platform what is coming and take them from idea to production — running daily on live utility networks — closely guided by experienced data scientists who know these systems well.

Some Of The Key Activities Will Include

Build and improve energy demand forecasting models (heat and cooling load) across a growing portfolio of utility networks and get them into production with automated retraining and minimal manual intervention.
Work on local weather and condition forecasting that outperforms global and regional models at individual network level — a proven differentiator we want to push further.
Make forecasting robust at scale: self-adaptive models, drift and anomaly detection, and forecast accuracy monitoring across many networks at once.
Blend physics with data — combine physical modelling principles of thermal systems with statistical and machine learning methods, rather than treating the network as a black box.
Build and develop the data pipelines your models depend on, together with our data engineering platform team.

The Team

Your main development team is based in Denmark, working with colleagues across several European locations. Beyond your daily team, you join a data science community in Denmark of experienced data scientists working on problems next to yours — production optimization, thermo-hydraulic network simulation, temperature optimization. You will have people to think out loud with, review your models and challenge your assumptions, and you will do the same for them.

What We're Looking For

You are a data scientist who wants to turn messy real-world problems into models that work in production, and who is curious about the physical systems behind the data.

Early in your career? Please apply. We care more about how you think than how many years you have. If you are at a junior level but determined to grow into a deep specialist — rigorous about model quality, curious about how energy systems actually behave, and keen to be challenged by people who know more than you do — we want to hear from you. You will be guided closely by experienced data scientists, and we will invest in getting you there.

On top of that, you should be able to checkmark some of the points listed below:

Hold a Master’s degree or higher in a relevant field (mathematics, machine learning, statistics, physics, etc.)
PhD degree is a benefit, but not a strict requirement
Previous experience of Python as this is used as our main programming tool, together with a solid foundation in statistics and machine learning — from studies, thesis work, internships or professional experience
Experience with forecasting and time-series modelling, especially models that have to run in production
Forecasting experience in energy systems or electricity markets is a plus
Experience with modern data pipelines and cloud-based data platforms

jobs.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands.

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth.

We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.

Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow.

For more information, visit WPP.com.

Why we're hiring:

Open Intelligence (OI) is one of WPP’s most strategic bets - a flagship data and AI initiative at the intersection of machine learning, advertising technology, and audience insight, built to power the next generation of media intelligence. Operating across the US and UK and expanding across EMEA and APAC, OI runs at true global scale.

To lead the next phase of development at the embedding and applied-AI layer of OI, we are hiring a Data Science Team Lead in Copenhagen. You will guide a small, sharp team building critical capabilities - from multimodal embedding spaces and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to agentic tools and UIs - that make the rest of OI’s AI ecosystem thrive.

What you'll be doing:

Line-manage and grow the team: Drive 1:1s, recruitment, performance, mentorship, and day-to-day technical and team direction.
Own technical architecture & direction: Lead the technical vision and design for well-distributed multimodal embedding spaces (text, image, video), MCP server tooling, and user-facing chat agents + UI.
Translate strategy into action: Take high-level, ambiguous direction from leadership and stakeholders, shape it into a clear narrative, and break it down into concrete, well-scoped projects.
Uphold a high engineering bar: Set and maintain high standards for clean architecture, system design, and testable code while keeping delivery pragmatic and incremental.
Communicate impact: Clearly articulate the team’s work, architectural decisions, and business value upward to leadership and across the wider Open Intelligence organization.
Stay hands-on: Keep close enough to the code and technical stack to make sound architectural calls, conduct code reviews, and unblock the team.

Who you'll be working with:

You’ll report directly to the Director of Data Science, Open Intelligence, and join our vibrant Copenhagen office of ~50 people, including 14+ data scientists and a strong engineering group.

We operate fluidly across closely collaborating teams. Our culture is flat, high-trust, and fast-moving: strong opinions loosely held, teamwork over ego, aiming high, and having fun along the way.

What you'll need:

Solid understanding of software architecture, system design, clean code principles, and testability. (We lean toward an engineering-minded lead, but strongly technical Data Scientists or ML Engineers with engineering instincts are very welcome).
Deep proficiency in Python and cloud experience (ideally GCP — Vertex AI, Cloud Run, BigQuery).
Hands-on experience with embeddings, vector search, LLM tooling, and agentic workflows (experience with MCP / Model Context Protocol is a strong plus).
Demonstrated ability to untangle ambiguity and turn broad goals into shipped, high-quality production systems.
Ability to shape complex technical concepts into compelling, easy-to-understand storylines for technical and non-technical stakeholders alike.

Note:
Direct people-leadership experience is a plus, but not a mandatory requirement if you have strong technical/project leadership instincts.

Success attributes:

You untangle ambiguity rather than being intimidated by it.
Pragmatic perfectionist: high standards, incremental delivery.
Low ego, high trust; you make the people around you better.
Thrive in a fast-paced, flat, entrepreneurial environment.

Who you are:

You're open :
We are inclusive and collaborative; we encourage the free exchange of ideas; we respect and celebrate diverse views. We are open-minded: to new ideas, new partnerships, new ways of working.

You're optimistic :
We believe in the power of creativity, technology and talent to create brighter futures or our people, our clients and our communities. We approach all that we do with conviction: to try the new and to seek the unexpected.

You're extraordinary:
we are stronger together: through collaboration we achieve the amazing. We are creative leaders and pioneers of our industry; we provide extraordinary every day.

What we'll give you:

Passionate, inspired people
– We aim to create a culture in which people can do extraordinary work.

Scale and opportunity
– We offer the opportunity to create, influence and complete projects at a scale that is unparalleled in the industry.

Challenging and stimulating work
– Unique work and the opportunity to join a group of creative problem solvers. Are you up for the challenge?

We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week.
